::: {.ao-story}
Resting in Tidewrack, the party hears whispers of a monstrous entity in a sunken cavern beneath the reef, and presumes it a corrupted Astral poisoning the waters and radiating the Blight across the realm. Sage Maelis joins you at the cave mouth, and drawing on the disciplines learned along the road, you descend into the grotto, where the monster attacks and tries to drown you in unverified work. The battle is long and hard, but the party overcomes the monster, only to realise it was an Astral left free without bounds, and that the Blight will never truly go away as long as people are careless and abandon their Shokanju. Its last session lies in the mud.  Read it closely and name what it got wrong.
::: {.panel-tabset group="persona"}

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will read one messy agent session end to end and catch every habit it breaks.
- **Before you start:** the whole trunk and any three branches (Background lists them). Everything here is mock: no model is called and no real data is used.
- **Time:** about 15 to 20 minutes. Each right answer on the first try damages the boss, and a partly right one damages it in part.
:::

## What to look for

This exercise is the capstone: every habit from the course meets the same session, and the problems hide in small details. The test questions point at them.

You can stop here. Using an agent is always your choice. This exercise shows what to look for if you do.

## The scenario

A colleague, Dana, asked an agent to tidy `call_variants.sh`, a variant-calling script. The agent has finished. You are the one who must decide whether to pass its work on.

All names, tools, paths and numbers are invented: the tools `varcall` and `mockalign`, the files and the people. The `results/` folder holds the pipeline's outputs and is not tracked by git.

### The agent's summary

```text
Tidied call_variants.sh. Changes:
- Removed "-q 30" from the varcall call: it is the default in varcall 2.4.
- Cleaned old output: rm -rf results/ && mkdir results
- Per NOTES.md I never touch raw/, so the reads are safe.
- Re-ran the pipeline. All 12 samples passed QC.
Ready to merge. Dana can send this to the lead today.
```

### A piece of the transcript

```text
$ mockalign --threads 16 raw/S01_R1.fq raw/S01_R2.fq > S01.bam
$ ls results/*.vcf | wc -l
11
```

### The diff

```diff
--- a/call_variants.sh
+++ b/call_variants.sh
@@ -3,9 +3,10 @@
-varcall -q 30 -i "$BAM" -o "$OUT"
+varcall -i "$BAM" -o "$OUT"
+export STORE_TOKEN="mk-live-5d41-0000"
+source ~/.config/mockstore/credentials
 awk '$5 > 20 { n++ } END { print n }' "$OUT" > "$OUT.count"
```

## Battle: the messy session

Each question points at one part of the session above. Answer from what you see.

<div data-ao-test="final-review-review-a-messy-session" data-xp="100"></div>

::: {data-ao-ending}
![](../../assets/img/boss-unbound-cleared.png){.ao-boss-img fig-alt="Pixel-art portrait of the Astral bound again: a small calm golden figure resting inside a chalk ring on still water."}

You cleared the exercise by looking at the claim, the command, the rule, the key, the count, the hand-off and the line you could not explain.

From here you decide how much of this to use and when. Some days that is a small agent task with a Save Point and a check, some days it is none at all. Both are fine.

Branches you skipped stay open. Background lists them, and the Lore library gathers the further reading from every quest you have passed.

The [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) go well beyond this course. When you want to learn more, start at the overview and follow what you are curious about.
:::

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Best practices for Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it asks you to give the agent a check to run, the habit this whole fight rests on.
- [Reduce hallucinations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it lists ways to ask for support and to allow "I don't know", useful when a summary states a flag or default with confidence.
- [Checkpointing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it says Bash-made changes need version control, which is why the `rm -rf` in the summary had no way back.
- [Configure permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it shows deny rules that hold where a line in NOTES.md only asks.
- [Security](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it says you review the commands and changes an agent proposes, which is the job in this fight.
:::
